$comment: Synthetic talent profiles. All people are fictional. `revealName` is the full name and `contact` mock personal info (example.com e-mail, placeholder phone number), revealed only after mutual opt-in. `audit` is self-declared group data used ONLY for the aggregate fairness check; it is never scored or shown in matching. The pool is deliberately varied by origin, language, education and career path. Skill ids refer to data/esco/skills.json. `alias` defaults to 'Candidate <id>'.

talent.headline: Registered nurse from Lagos, in the Finnish licensing process for nurses trained abroad.

evidence.prompt: A patient refuses their evening medication. What do you do?
evidence.excerpt: Sit down, ask what worries them, check if it's side effects or confusion, then document and inform the doctor rather than pushing.

evidence.prompt: 60-second voice note: working with people from many backgrounds
evidence.excerpt: On my ward we had patients speaking five languages. I learned to use pictures and family members carefully, and to check understanding twice.

talent.headline: Practical nurse with 15 years in home care. Calm under pressure.

evidence.prompt: You arrive and a client is confused and hasn't eaten. First steps?
evidence.excerpt: Check blood sugar and fluids, look for signs of infection, call the nurse on duty, and leave a clear note for the next visit.

talent.headline: Front-end developer who tests with screen readers before shipping.

evidence.prompt: Small work sample
evidence.excerpt: Rebuilt a date picker so it's fully keyboard-navigable; documented ARIA decisions in the PR.

evidence.prompt: A designer hands you a low-contrast mockup. What do you do?
evidence.excerpt: Show them the contrast ratio next to WCAG AA, suggest two token tweaks, and ship with their sign-off.

talent.headline: Grew up in Espoo; six years on the warehouse floor, the last two as acting shift lead.

evidence.prompt: 60-second voice note: a shift that went wrong
evidence.excerpt: Two pickers called in sick before a big order. I re-split zones by SKU weight, took a scanner myself, and we shipped 20 minutes late instead of two hours.

talent.headline: Logistics coordinator who keeps carriers, customers and the warehouse on the same page.

evidence.prompt: A truck is stuck at the border and the customer is calling. What do you do?
evidence.excerpt: Get a realistic ETA from the driver first, then call the customer with two options: partial delivery from local stock or a new slot tomorrow.

talent.headline: Former chef, now a self-taught back-end developer who writes tests first.

evidence.prompt: Small work sample
evidence.excerpt: A small Django API for a food bank's pickup schedule, with tests for double bookings.

evidence.prompt: 60-second voice note: what your old job taught you
evidence.excerpt: A kitchen at 8 pm is a production incident every night. You learn to call things out early and never leave your station messy.

talent.headline: Moves messy sensor data into tidy, queryable tables.

evidence.prompt: A sensor feed suddenly doubles in volume. What do you do first?
evidence.excerpt: Check whether it's real load or duplicated messages: I'd sample timestamps per device, then add idempotent keys at ingest so reprocessing is safe.

evidence.prompt: Small work sample
evidence.excerpt: Wrote a 40-line Python parser for CAN-bus logs with tests for malformed frames.

talent.headline: Nurse turned health informatics specialist; speaks both clinician and developer.

evidence.prompt: Developers want to reuse patient notes to train a triage model. What do you ask first?
evidence.excerpt: What's the legal basis and is it secondary use under Findata rules? Then: can we do it with structured fields only, pseudonymised, before touching free text?

talent.headline: Former teacher turned junior data analyst.

evidence.prompt: 60-second voice note: explain something technical simply
evidence.excerpt: I explained median vs mean to parents using bus delays — one very late bus shouldn't change how you plan your morning.

evidence.prompt: Small work sample
evidence.excerpt: Notebook analysing school-meal waste by weekday; suggested menu swaps that cut waste ~20%.

talent.headline: Recent Aalto MSc graduate; builds forecasting models people actually use.

evidence.prompt: Small work sample
evidence.excerpt: Thesis model forecasting district-heating demand 24 h ahead; beat the utility's baseline by 11% MAE and shipped as a nightly job.

talent.headline: HVAC technician who can explain a ventilation fault to any tenant.

evidence.prompt: Residents complain an apartment block is stuffy every evening. Where do you look?
evidence.excerpt: Check the AHU schedule first — often it steps down at 17:00 for an office pattern. Then filters and exhaust balancing per stairwell.

talent.headline: Ten years running a warehouse floor, now learning to automate it with data.

evidence.prompt: 60-second voice note: a decision you changed with numbers
evidence.excerpt: We moved fast-moving SKUs closer to packing after I pulled pick-path data. Picking time dropped about 15%.

evidence.prompt: Write a query to find late shipments per carrier.
evidence.excerpt: GROUP BY carrier with a HAVING on late ratio; flagged that timestamps are local time so I'd normalise them first.

talent.headline: Pharmacist from Baghdad retraining in Finland; strong on medication safety.

evidence.prompt: An elderly client has prescriptions from three doctors. What worries you?
evidence.excerpt: Interactions and duplicates — I'd list every active substance, check for two drugs of the same class, and ask the GP for one medication review.

talent.headline: QA engineer who automates the boring checks so humans can test the weird stuff.

evidence.prompt: Small work sample
evidence.excerpt: Playwright suite with axe-core checks on every PR; cut regression testing from two days to 40 minutes.

talent.headline: Building services engineer, energy audits for older housing companies.

evidence.prompt: A housing company board is sceptical about a heat-pump retrofit. How do you explain it?
evidence.excerpt: Start from their annual heating bill, show payback in years, and bring one reference building they can visit.

talent.headline: Ex-barista, bootcamp UX designer. Runs usability tests in cafés.

evidence.prompt: Small work sample
evidence.excerpt: Redesigned a library booking flow after five guerrilla tests; task time fell from 3 min to 50 s.

evidence.prompt: 60-second voice note: what your old job taught you
evidence.excerpt: You read a queue in seconds — who's in a hurry, who's confused. That's half of user research.

talent.headline: Freight dispatcher from Tallinn; keeps 40 trucks moving through bad weather.

evidence.prompt: A snowstorm closes the main road at 6 am. What's your first hour?
evidence.excerpt: Re-route the three most time-critical loads, warn customers with honest ETAs, and keep one driver in reserve for whatever breaks next.

talent.headline: Electrician with solar and battery installation experience.

evidence.prompt: A battery inverter keeps tripping at noon. Possible causes?
evidence.excerpt: Peak PV output exceeding inverter rating, a loose DC connection heating up, or wrong grid-code setting after an update.

talent.headline: Cloud security analyst; thinks about what could go wrong so others don't have to.

evidence.prompt: You find an S3 bucket with patient exports set to public. What now?
evidence.excerpt: Lock it immediately, snapshot access logs before they rotate, then tell the DPO — 72-hour GDPR clock may already be running.

talent.headline: Ex-Defence Forces logistics NCO moving into civilian project management.

evidence.prompt: 60-second voice note: a plan you had to change
evidence.excerpt: Exercise supplies for 300 people, and the ferry was cancelled. We split loads across two routes and briefed every team lead the same evening.

talent.headline: Supply-chain planner who loves a good spreadsheet model.

evidence.prompt: A key supplier announces a 6-week delay. Walk us through your first day.
evidence.excerpt: Quantify stock cover per SKU, rank customers by impact, then call two alternates with a pre-filled RFQ.

talent.headline: Caregiver with eight years in assisted living in Manila and Espoo.

evidence.prompt: A resident with dementia becomes agitated during a shower. What do you do?
evidence.excerpt: Stop, lower my voice, give them a towel to hold, and try again later or with a colleague they trust. Note what triggered it.

talent.headline: Ex-musician, self-taught analyst who makes dashboards people open on Mondays.

evidence.prompt: Small work sample
evidence.excerpt: Ticket-sales dashboard for a festival: SQL on the box-office DB, one page, three numbers the producer actually asked for.

talent.headline: Full-stack bootcamp graduate with a background in customer support.

evidence.prompt: Users say the form 'doesn't work'. How do you investigate?
evidence.excerpt: Reproduce on their device, check the console and network tab, then ask one specific question instead of 'what happened?'.

talent.headline: Sustainability coordinator who made ESG reporting less painful.

evidence.prompt: Your CEO wants emissions numbers by Friday. What do you send?
evidence.excerpt: Scope 1–2 from invoices we already have, a clear note on what's estimated, and a plan for Scope 3 next quarter.

talent.headline: Cloud data engineer, likes boring reliable pipelines.

evidence.prompt: Small work sample
evidence.excerpt: Terraform + dbt project that loads open energy-price data hourly with freshness alerts.

talent.headline: Ten years in grocery retail, now moving into warehouse work and logistics.

evidence.prompt: A delivery arrives two hours late and the evening shift is short-staffed. What do you do?
evidence.excerpt: Unload the chilled goods first, move one person from the tills to receiving, and tell the shift manager which shelves will be late.

evidence.prompt: 60-second voice note: a difficult customer
evidence.excerpt: A customer was shouting about a missing order. I listened, found the box in the back room and offered to carry it to the car.

talent.headline: Data engineer from Izmir, five years building batch and streaming pipelines.

evidence.prompt: A nightly data job silently drops 3% of rows. How do you find out why?
evidence.excerpt: Compare row counts at each step, log the rejected rows instead of dropping them, and add a test that fails when counts don't match.

evidence.prompt: Short code sample
evidence.excerpt: A Python job that deduplicates sensor readings by device and timestamp before loading them, with a retry on network errors.

talent.headline: Former primary school teacher who retrained as a front-end developer at a bootcamp.

evidence.prompt: A form works for you but a user says they can't submit it. What do you check?
evidence.excerpt: Check the console, try it with the keyboard only, check validation messages, and reproduce in their browser before changing any React state logic.

evidence.prompt: 60-second voice note: explaining something hard
evidence.excerpt: I taught fractions to eight-year-olds. Now I pair with junior devs the same way: one small step, then let them drive.

talent.headline: HVAC installer with a vocational degree, eight years on renovation sites.

evidence.prompt: A building's heating bill rose 20% after a renovation. Where do you start?
evidence.excerpt: Check the ventilation heat recovery settings and the radiator balancing first; after renovations they are often left at factory defaults.

evidence.prompt: 60-second voice note: something that went wrong
evidence.excerpt: A pump kept failing. Instead of replacing it a third time I traced it to a valve installed backwards upstream.

talent.headline: Practical nurse trained in Finland, four years in home care and assisted living.

evidence.prompt: An elderly client living alone seems more confused than last week. What do you do?
evidence.excerpt: Check whether medicines were taken as dosed, look for signs of infection or dehydration, write it down and call the nurse on duty the same day.

evidence.prompt: 60-second voice note: a good day at work
evidence.excerpt: A client who never talked started telling me about her garden. I came ten minutes early each visit so we had time for it.

talent.headline: Moved from freight forwarding into supply chain analytics after a master's degree.

evidence.prompt: Stock-outs of one product doubled last quarter. How do you investigate?
evidence.excerpt: Pull weekly demand and lead times per supplier, see whether demand spiked or deliveries slipped, then adjust the reorder point with purchasing.

evidence.prompt: 60-second voice note: your previous job
evidence.excerpt: I booked trucks and containers across Central Europe, so I know where shipments actually get stuck at borders and ports.

talent.headline: Clinical research coordinator with hospital data and GDPR experience.

evidence.prompt: A study export from the patient record system has missing visit dates. What do you do?
evidence.excerpt: Flag the records, check the source entries in the patient record system with the ward, and log every correction so the audit trail stays intact.

evidence.prompt: Short work sample
evidence.excerpt: A one-page summary comparing readmission rates by ward, with the method and its limits stated in plain words.

talent.headline: Session musician turned software tester, self-taught with a testing certificate.

evidence.prompt: A bug only happens sometimes. How do you report it?
evidence.excerpt: Write exact steps, browser and time, attach a recording, and note what I tried that did not trigger it so developers can narrow it down.

evidence.prompt: 60-second voice note: working in a team
evidence.excerpt: In a band nobody plays louder to win. In testing I try the same thing: raise the issue, then help fix it.

talent.headline: Energy engineer from Kharkiv, did building energy audits and sustainability reports.

evidence.prompt: A client wants to cut their office's energy use by 15%. What is your plan?
evidence.excerpt: Measure a baseline for a month, find the biggest loads, start with no-cost fixes like schedules and setpoints, then price the bigger upgrades.

evidence.prompt: Short work sample
evidence.excerpt: Section of an annual sustainability report on scope 2 emissions, with the data sources listed.

talent.headline: Former bank clerk who taught himself SQL and data analysis online.

evidence.prompt: Your manager asks which products customers stop using first. How do you answer?
evidence.excerpt: Write a SQL query for the last use date per product per customer, group by product, and show the drop-off month by month in a simple chart.

evidence.prompt: 60-second voice note: your previous job
evidence.excerpt: At the bank I explained loan terms to people who were nervous about money. I learned to check they really understood, not just nodded.

talent.headline: Registered nurse moving into clinical data after training as an EHR super-user.

evidence.prompt: Nurses keep entering the same field in two places in the record system. What do you do?
evidence.excerpt: Watch a few shifts to see why, then show the system team where the duplicate entry happens and suggest one field with a clear label.

evidence.prompt: 60-second voice note: a busy shift
evidence.excerpt: In the emergency department I learned to keep talking to the patient while working, so they know what is happening.

talent.headline: Warehouse team lead from Bogotá, ran night shifts at a distribution centre.

evidence.prompt: Two of your eight pickers call in sick at the start of a night shift. What do you do?
evidence.excerpt: Prioritise the orders with the earliest trucks, pick myself on the busiest aisle, and ask the day lead to start one person an hour early.

evidence.prompt: 60-second voice note: a big change
evidence.excerpt: When we moved to a new scanner system overnight, I wrote a one-page cheat sheet in Spanish and English for the team.

talent.headline: UX designer from Gothenburg focused on accessible public-sector services.

evidence.prompt: Users abandon a sign-up form halfway. How do you find out why?
evidence.excerpt: Watch five people use it, check it with a screen reader, and look at which field they leave on before redesigning anything.

evidence.prompt: 60-second voice note: disagreeing with a stakeholder
evidence.excerpt: A manager wanted more fields. I showed a clip of a user giving up and we agreed to ask two questions later instead.

talent.headline: Architect from Beirut retraining in building energy efficiency.

evidence.prompt: An old school building is cold near the windows but too hot in the corridors. What do you suggest?
evidence.excerpt: Map the temperatures room by room, check window seals and where the heat is actually going, then propose fixes in order of cost.

evidence.prompt: Short work sample
evidence.excerpt: Schedule and budget for a three-month facade renovation, with the risks and who owns each one.
